newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmaker offers Internet, cellular bills.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmaker offers Internet, cellular bills.

text.p: A leading House lawmaker introduced three separate bills Wednesday designed to prevent cellular phone eavesdropping, new regulations on the Internet, and the unauthorized release of personal information obtained from cyberspace and intended for commercial use.

"As we prepeare to enter the 21st century, the Internet and cellular telephones have become two of the world's most important communications tools," said Rep. W.J. (Billy) Tauzin, a Louisiana Republican who chairs the telecommunications subcommittee.

The Internet Protection Act legislation would prohibit the regulation of rates, charges, practices, classifications, faciliities or services for -- or in connection with -- Internet information services.
The Wireless Privacy Enhancement Act legislation would bar the modification of scanners for the purpose of intercepting private cellular phone conversations.
The measure stems from the uproar earlier this year over House Speaker Newt Gingrich's intercepted cell-phone call.

The third bill, the Data Privacy Act, would require the interactive computer service industry to develop voluntary guidelines for the notification of consuemrs prior to the collection of "personally identifiable information."
Such information can include phone numbers and street addresses, for example.
